title: The Gift of the Prodigal
author: Peter Taylor
logline: An elderly man realizes his troublesome son is the only thing keeping him going.

title: A Fresno Fable
author: William Saroyan
logline: A grocer in desperate need of help enlists a lawyer to fix his problems, though he refuses to trust the lawyer enough to actually receive help.

title: Cinderella School
author: Lara Vapnyar
logline: An immigrant Russian woman gets a job teaching English classes out of a witch doctor's tiny Brooklyn office.

title: Girl
author: Jamaica Kincaid
logline: A Caribbean mother rants to her elementary-aged daughter about how to be a respectable girl. When the girls tries to reply, the mother continues her lecture.

title: Some People Are Just Plumb Crazy
author: Arthur Kober
logline: A restaurant owners tells a customer about a crazy client he once had.

title: Art of Story
author: John Edgar Wideman
logline: In 2018, a pedestrian on the New York City’s Lower East Side witnesses a young Black couple in love, prompting a consideration about the storytelling, hope, and Nelson Mandela.

title: Subpoena
author: Donald Barthelme
logline: A man is subpoenaed by Bureau of Compliance for not paying tax on the weekly allowance he gives a cyborg companion he built from human and machine parts. Unable to pay the outrageous tax and fee, he is forced to dissemble his ever-agreeable companion.

title: Adventure
author: Emily Hahn
logline: An American continues to run into another American on their trips around Europe and the Mediterranean.

title: Winter Night
author: Kay Boyle
logline: A neglected little girl conjures memories of her babysitter's tragic past. Just for the night, the two find an antidote to loss in each other.

title: This is a Love Story
author: Leane Zugsmith
logline: A mother saves up to buy an expensive gift for her absent son, hoping he will come home soon - but a chance conversation with strangers on the train forces her to come to terms with the reality that she may never see him again.

title: The Hanging of the Schoolmarm
author: Robert Coover
logline: A schoolmarm attempts to teach a group of men about justice, time, and irony in a repurposed saloon after they vote to have her hung for her disciplinarian ways.

title: More Like a Coffin
author: Hazel Hawthorne
logline: In the midst of World War II, a mother is forced to chaperone some young girls and witnesses the effect of the war in unexpected places.

title: The First Face
author: Elizabeth Enright
logline: A new mother wakes up after giving birth to her son and upon gazing at his face, feels an ephemeral peace that only comes once in a lifetime.

title: The Faithful Wife
author: Morley Callaghan
logline: A young station worker is infatuated with a woman he generally sees at a restaurant. He's never talked to her, but one day the woman tells him to come to her house.

title: The Cradle of Civilization
author: Dorothy Parker
logline: An American woman and man visiting France criticize the French people and culture, revealing their ignorance and disregard even as they delight in the fun their unusual group of friends is having.

title: Happy Trails
author: Sherman Alexie
logline: After his uncle goes missing, a young Coeur d'Alene Native American convinces his mom to hold a funeral. He reflects on all the family members he has lost and on their proximity to violence inflicted by the US government that is often viewed as past.

title: The pelican's shadow
author: Marjorie Kinnan Rawlings
logline: A newly married woman’s struggles with her husband’s narcissistic behavior manifest in her dislike for the pelicans on the beach.

title: A Game of Catch
author: Richard Wilbur
logline: When two seventh graders refuse to let another boy into their game of catch, the spurned boy uses his magic powers to get what he wants.

title: Pet Milk
author: Stuart Dybeck
logline: When a Chicago man decides to add Pet Milk to his coffee, the old-fashioned dairy product stirs up memories of his polka-loving grandmother and his beautiful college girlfriend.

title: I See You Never
author: Ray Bradbury
logline: A landlady says a tearful farewell to one of her Mexican tenants, who must leave due to an expired visa.

title: The School
author: Donald Barthelme
logline:
A series of deaths leave students wondering about life. 

After watching their class's pet gerbil, fish and plants die, the students are left wondering if their school is cursed.

title: Margins
author: Donald Barthelme
logline: An insufferable white man offers advice to a well-read, unemployed Black man holding a sandwich-board sign on a street corner on race relations, physical appearance, and how to improve his handwriting and thereby advance himself in society.

title: The Valet of the Splendide
author: Ludwig Bemelmans
logline: The owner of an expensive hotel employs a poor musician as his assistant. The owner begins to bond with his new servant and becomes wary when the musician begins to focus his attention on better opportunities.

title: Look at a Teacup
author: Patricia Hampl
logline: During her conversations with her mother, a daughter often muses about the past, both politically and personally. She discovers more about her mother but also about the world around her as she observes life and its souvenirs.

title: The Most Elegant Drawing Room in Europe
author: Nancy Hale
logline: A shy American librarian and her abrasive mother travel to Italy, where a visit with a beautiful Italian countess stirs up the daughter's insecurity about her terrible teeth — and re-animates her rage at her mother, who neglected to have them fixed.

title: Man and Woman
author: Erskine Caldwell
logline: An exhausted husband and wife travel by foot and stop by a house to ask a woman for food. She is rude and only allows the wife to eat, but the wife saves some food for her husband so they can continue their long journey.

title: Search Through the Streets of the City
author: Irwin Shaw
logline: A man who hasn't gotten over his past love, sees his ex walking down the streets. The only issue is that the ex has changed and is married.

title: Passing Through
author: Robert M. Coates
logline: In an East Ohio town, a middle-aged man checks into a hotel and explores the various characters, events and surroundings that define small town life.

title: The Voyage Out
author: Morley Callaghan
logline: A young man, enthusiastic about his new love interest, soon realizes he has an issue with staring at the women around him and driving them away.

title: Still of Some Use
author: John Updike
logline: As a wistful divorcee helps his ex-wife and two sons clear out their former home, discarding nostalgic belongings, he finds it difficult to let go of the past.

title: Game
author: Donald Barthelme
logline: Two men have been locked underground somewhere in Utah, Montana, or Idaho with instructions to wait for a monitor's signal then each turn a key in a lock simultaneously to fire a "bird" at an unknown target city. They also have guns and instructions to shoot the other if the other behaves strangely.

title: Only the Dead Know Brooklyn
author: Thomas Wolfe
logline: A native Brooklynite helps a big man get to Boisenhoist, a section in Brooklyn. However, as the two converse, the native Brooklynite becomes more and more wary of the other man's antics.

title: Suite 2049
author: Sally Benson
logline: A woman who lives happily in hotel rooms is shaken when her husband suddenly decides he wants a new life.

title: The Shawl
author: Cynthia Ozick
logline: A starving young teenager struggles to survive with her infant on their march towards a Nazi concentration camp. However, another prisoner plots to steal the teenage mom's magical shawl on which the infant relies.

title: The jockey
author: Carson McCullers
logline: A jockey becomes heated after a big race and disrespects those around him.

title: The Second Tree from the Corner
author: E. B. White
logline: A patient attends regular sessions with his psychiatrist but stubbornly refuses to tell the doctor his true thoughts.

title: The Professor's Houses
author: Ursula K. Le Guin
logline: A professor becomes obsessed with his daughter's dollhouse, and he crafts its furniture, keeps it neat and organized, and envisions himself inside it, even after his daughter grows up and leaves for college.

title: Sunday Lunch
author: Nancy Hale
logline: In the 1960s, a old woman, her son, and her daughter-in-law host guests for Sunday lunch. The woman thinks she has kept the nuclear shelter beneath the house secret from her son, with whom she has a strained relationship. However, her son knows and has installed a back way in, such that he can surprise her there after she locks herself inside.

title: The Apostate
author: George Milburn
logline: In an epistolary-like work, a father must choose between a job he loves and his relationship with his son.

title: Buttony
author: Fiona McFarlane
logline: A young schoolteacher leads her class through a game where they have to figure out who has the button, until the class cannot find the button.

title: What Do You See, Dear Enid?
author: Grace Flandrau
logline: A young girl stays with a bizarre family that has magical powers. As strange things happen to the family members, the girl starts to believe that the family lineage will die out.

title: The Red Hat
author: Morley Callaghan
logline: A woman whose husband is out of work buys an expensive hat and hopes that her husband will let her keep it. But when her husband tells her to get rid of it, the woman obliges, all the while hoping she can buy it back.

title: Solstice
author: Anne Enright
logline: After he loses his mother, a father feels unmoored and lashes out at his family as the winter solstice arrives.

title: Utopia of a Tired Man
author: Jorge Luis Borges and Norman Thomas di Giovanni (Translator)
logline: A man who can travel through time and space finds himself a houseguest in the distant future.

title: Honeymoon
author: Arturo Vivante
logline: After building their dream rural life together in the mountains, a humble couple goes into Rome for their honeymoon and begins to question if their partner would be more satisfied with someone resembling the modern city dwellers around them.

title: A City of Churches
author: Donald Barthelme
logline: A woman looks for a place to live in a town entirely comprised of churches, (but discovers...)

title: Back the Way You Went
author: Anne Carson
logline: A woman's complicated relationship to her mother is captured in three vignettes: one from directly after her death, one from when she is still alive, and one from years after she is gone.

title: First Marriage
author: St. Clair McKelway
logline: A man tells his assistant about his first marriage when they go on a business trip to Chicago after the company opens up a new branch in the building he used to live in with his first wife.

title: Deaths of Distant Friends
author: John Updike
logline: A middle-aged, divorced man learns of three deaths of people he once knew. The news of each brings him slight relief from the shame he feels about his failed marriage.

title: Collectors
author: Daniel Alarcón
logline: In 1980s Peru, a dyslexic drug trafficker and grade school dropout and a wealthy, famous playwright labeled a terrorist for his play about killing the president form an unlikely relationship as cellmates in the notorious Collectors Prison of San Jacinto. The playwright convinces the men in their block to stage a performance of the play that landed him in jail, bringing a sense of comradery and unity; however, months after his release, he learns that the entire block, including his lover, was killed in the military suppression of a prison revolt.

title: Collectors
author: Daniel Alarcón
logline: In 1980s Peru, a dyslexic drug trafficker and grade school dropout and a wealthy, famous playwright labeled a terrorist for his play about killing the president form an unlikely relationship as cellmates in the notorious Collectors Prison of San Jacinto. The playwright convinces the men in their block to stage a performance of the play that landed him in jail, bringing a sense of comradery and unity; however, months after his release, he learns that the entire block, including his lover, was killed in the military suppression of a prison revolt.

title: 5135 Kensington: August, 1903
author: Sally Benson
logline: A young woman tries to attract the attention of a colonel so that she can live a comfortable life.

title: The Man Who Loved Extinct Mammals
author: John Updike
logline: A man intently studies extinct mammals to escape his wife and mistress, who often vent to him about their daily worries and give him anxiety.

title: Everything Is Far From Here
author: Cristina Henríquez
logline: When a mother crosses the United States southern border to escape the unsafe conditions of her home country, she begins having psychotic episodes while she waits to be reunited with her five-year-old son, from whom she was separated during the journey.

title: Trash
author: Souvankham Thammavongsa
logline: A married woman ponders the kindness and subsequent coldness of her mother-in-law.

title: My Brother Osong's Career in Politics
author: Carlos Bulosan
logline: When a father-son duo uses their political power to transform an old Philippine town, they overspend the town's budget and must find a way to quickly recover the money.

title: A Local Skirmish
author: Noel Houston
logline: When a small neighborhood starts practicing air raid drills for World War II, a new German couple down the block stirs up trouble for themselves when they get into a spat with their neighbors.

title: Janus
author: Ann Beattie
logline: A real estate agent obsesses over a bowl gifted by her secret lover. Over time, she becomes more infatuated with the bowl and less infatuated with her lover, yet she still must decide if she should end her marriage to be with him.

title: Son
author: John Updike
logline: A series of vignettes about various sons along a family tree.

title: Referential
author: Lorrie Moore
logline: A middle-aged woman is forced to grapple with her son’s mental illness and her partner’s disinterest. While she tries to accommodate everyone else, the woman begins to lose herself.

title: The Pleasures of Solitude
author: John Cheever
logline: A self-reliant but lonely woman becomes excited by the incidental visit of two boys in her apartment. When she unwisely lends them her long-buried trust and kindness, she quickly regrets it.

title: Come Dance With Me in Ireland
author: Shirley Jackson
logline: In twentieth century Ireland, three women decide to impart their generosity on an old man, but their bad manners and hosting skills are not well received by their charity case.

title: Andrew
author: Berry Morgan
logline: In a rural Mississippi town, a well-intentioned Black woman tries to help a clueless young white mother take care of her baby, but the mother's family gets in the way.

title: The Eldest Child
author: Maeve Brennan
logline: A young mother mourns the death of her firstborn child, a son, three days after his birth and falls into a bout of depression.

title: Fellow-Creatures
author: Wright Morris
logline: A retired U.S. Army colonel develops an unexpected appreciation for the animal life around him, which leads him to make significant changes to his own life.

title: An Afternoon
author: Elizabeth Warner
logline: When an old nurse and two children go out for a perfect afternoon walk, they are distraught to return home and find that something is out of place.

title: La Vita Nuova
author: Allegra Goodman
logline: After an elementary school art teacher's fiancé breaks up with her and calls off the wedding, the Yale graduate gets fired from her job and begins babysitting one of her former first graders.

title: The cane in the corridor
author: James Thurber
logline: Three people all sit down to talk after a night of drinking, but the agenda of one dinner guest changes the night.

title: Uncle Rock
author: Dagoberto Gilb
logline: After imagining his single mother would marry the wealthy engineer she was previously dating, the young, silent son of a Mexican-American immigrant finds himself irrationally disliking the kind, doting, and very average man she thinks she might marry. When an opportunity comes to sabotage the relationship, will he take it?

title: Kingdom Come
author: Mavis Gallant
logline: An old linguistics researcher is ousted from his university position on the frontier of a small island he acculturated. Upon his return home, he begins to believe that he and his life's work are marginal.

title: Houdini
author: Jerome Weidman
logline: Two strict Boy Scout scoutmasters decide to prank a third scoutmaster who is loved by the boys. In doing so, they put his authority with the boys into question.

title: Love Letter
author: George Saunders
logline: A grandfather writes a letter to his grandson at some point in 2020’s. His grandson wants to know about someone referred to as J, but he implores Robbie to stay away from her through his recollections and realizations about family love.

title: Nothing Ever Breaks Except the Heart
author: Kay Boyle
logline: A woman trying to get a flight to America begins to spend time with the attendant who booked her flight and learns about his personal history.

title: Playing Metal Gear Solid V: The Phantom Pain
author: Jamil Jan Kochai
logline: A young Afghani immigrant boy plays a war video game set in a Soviet-controlled Afghanistan. The game reminds him of his parents who fled the war, and he begins to imagine himself rescuing his uncle, a man who died in battle.

title: The Custodian
author: Deborah Eisenberg
logline: Lynnie is a young, working-class girl who works at the Stone House in town and wastes her days making stories about the lives of the people around her, which she tells to her friend, Isobel. But when rumors start to circulate, Isobel mysteriously moves away, and Lynnie is left wondering why.

title: Exiles From the Creuse
author: Mary Mian
logline: While visiting Paris for the holiday season, a young girl and her grandfather get homesick for the countryside. At the Christmas market, they finally find something worth coming to the city for.

title: Alan Bean Plus Four
author: Tom Hanks
logline: A millennial in an unnamed American city recruits his girlfriend, his friend, and his friend's Home Depot coworker on a mission to circle around the moon.

title: In the Words of
author: Julie Hayden
logline: An ex-couple spends the afternoon together catching up in a valley they used to call their own, a month after the man loses his job. He paints, and she watches birds.

title: The Crabapple Tree
author: Robert Coover
logline: There is something suspicious about the family with a crabapple tree on their property.  After a new stepmother arrives, the other members of the family start to mysteriously drop like flies.

title: Black Secret
author: Marjorie Kinnan Rawlings
logline: A seven-year-old plantation heir overhears his mother and her friend discuss the allure of black women. He then discovers a dark secret about his family tree, which leads him to a breaking point.

title: Jealous Husband Returns in Form of Parrot
author: Robert Olen Butler
logline: A man who was a jealous husband in his past life now inhabits the body of a parrot. His wife buys him from a pet store, and he is forced to watch her from his cage as she brings other men home, again and again.

title: Preach on the Dusty Roads
author: Irwin Shaw
logline: After an accountant finishes helping his company evade taxes, he says goodbye to his son leaving for war.

title: Along the Frontage Road
author: Michael Chabon
logline: A man takes his four-year-old son to a pumpkin patch, where they encounter another father-son duo.

title: The Catbird Seat
author: James Thurber
logline: When a man believes his job is at risk because of an annoying, incompetent woman at his office, he decides to take drastic action to end her influence once and for all.

title: The Boundary
author: Jhumpa Lahiri
logline: The 15-year-old daughter of immigrants works as a keeper for a rural cottage with her parents. She observes the family who takes over the cottage for a week.

title: The Young Priest
author: Morley Callaghan
logline: A young priest who sees the world through rose-colored glasses admires an older woman dedicated to the parish. When she requests that he visit her, his overly optimistic expectations of churchgoers, and his honor of being a young clergyman, are challenged.

title: Walking Wounded
author: Irwin Shaw
logline: A young soldier grapples with the idea that his wife may have forgotten him while he is stationed in a city where women are leaving their husbands for men nearby.

title: Bulldog
author: Arthur Miller
logline: Set around the 1940s, a thirteen-year-old boy pursues the purchase of a puppy he saw in a newspaper ad, and receives an unexpected sexual experience from the woman who sells him the dog.

title: Tib's Eve
author: Ellen Currie
logline: A teenage girl at a boarding school faces expulsion and punishment from her indifferent parents. She gets into an unlikely conversation with the school janitor, who tells her he used to know her mother, and surprises her with what he has to say.

title: Shoe the Horse and Shoe the Mare
author: Astrid Meighan
logline: When a teenage girl meets with her father to remind him of his late alimony payments, she feels disappointed by his unhelpful reaction.

title: Shoe the Horse and Shoe the Mare
author: Astrid Meighan
logline: When a teenage girl meets with her father to remind him of his late alimony payments, she feels disappointed by his unhelpful reaction.

title: Flower Hunters
author: Lauren Groff
logline: After getting dumped by her best friend, a woman stays home alone on Halloween to find solace in the writing of an 18th-century naturalist.

title: bohemians
author: George Saunders
logline: A group of kids in a Chicago neighborhood direct both spite and love at two old women who are not who they seem.

title: Earthquake Damage
author: Alice Adams
logline: A woman flying home to San Francisco is forced on a detour because of a catastrophic earthquake that hits Northern California. She calls an ex-boyfriend with whom she is still in love to make sure he is safe and the two weigh whether or not to continue their romance.

title: Tib's Eve
author: Ellen Currie
logline: A teenage girl at a boarding school faces expulsion and punishment from her indifferent parents. She gets into an unlikely conversation with the school janitor, who tells her he used to know her mother, and surprises her with what he has to say.

title: Basil From Her Garden
author: Donald Barthelme
logline: In a lengthy dialogue, two men, possibly a psychologist and a patient, discuss adultery, sin, desire, and life.

title: Diary of an Interesting Year
author: Helen Simpson
logline: A 33-year-old woman living in an apocalyptic Scotland with her husband writes in her diary about the tribulations of their lives and their pilgrimage to Russia in hope of a more stable existence.

title: Flight Through the Dark
author: Roger Angell
logline: A man takes a stressful plane ride back home from a business trip in Washington. He is highly disturbed by his sleep-walking incident in the hotel and struggles to fight negative thoughts about the war and his unhappy sister.

title: Writing Teacher
author: John Edgar Wideman
logline: A creative writing teacher sits through a conference with one his favorite students. He takes us on a journey through the characters in the story, and in his life.

title: The Net
author: Robert M. Coates
logline: After a man sees his ex-wife with another man on the street, he follows her home and his rage overtakes him, making him do something he regrets.

title: Puppy
author: George Saunders
logline: When a mother takes her children to buy a puppy from another mother, she finds an unsettling household and a child chained like a dog in the backyard. Through their alternating narratives, both mothers reflect on what it means to love your children.

title: The Lottery
author: Shirley Jackson
logline: In a small American village, anticipation builds for an annual event dubbed "The Lottery," where villagers select a member of the community at random to suffer an irrational and inhumane fate.

title: Brothers and Sisters Around the World
author: Andrea Lee
logline: A mystic woman rules over her island and recounts the journey she took to get there. From Boston as a young, Black girl to a wealthy French estate owner, nobody can seem to take their eyes off of her.

title: My Brother's Second Funeral
author: Edward Newhouse
logline: During WWII, a lieutenant's death prompts his father to plan an unnecessarily theatric funeral. The late lieutenant's brother is disgusted, knowing the dead man would have hated such an empty gesture.

title: Other People's Deaths
author: Lore Segal
logline: A deceased man’s friends and coworkers try to come up with the best way to mourn him and comfort his widow, even though it seems like she doesn’t need it.

title: Paper Losses
author: Lorrie Moore
logline: When a former anti-war nudist files for divorce from his hippie-turned-middle-aged conservative wife, a figurative nuclear war fires up between the two suburban parents.

title: Awaiting Orders
author: Tobias Wolff
logline: A homosexual military sergeant, with no use for his money after his parent’s estrangement, attempts to support the destitute family of a soldier just shipped off to Iraq.

title: Kattekoppen
author: Will Mackin
logline: While a howitzer liaison for an American military unit in Afghanistan returns home on parental leave, his unit embarks on a mission to find two missing soldiers and finds a possibly permanent replacement for him.

title: The Big Cat
author: Louise Erdrich
logline: A two-bit actor who married into a family of female snorers wades through a messy divorce, remarries, and endures another, messier, divorce from his second ex-wife. He finally lands back with his original family—a wife who he knows doesn’t love him and a daughter who has also begun to snore.

title: The Fragments
author: Joshua Ferris
logline: After a man finds out his wife is having an affair from a butt dial, he invites strangers walking on the street into his apartment to chat and ease his turmoil.

title: Marriage Quarantine
author: Kate Walbert
logline: In the quarantine stage of the 2020 pandemic, a woman and her husband reflect on their marriage, how time has somehow conflated, making them, at once, who they are now and who they used to be.

title: Separating
author: John Updike
logline: A married couple has decided to separate, but first they must go through the difficult task of telling their four children.

title: Other People's Deaths
author: Lore Segal
logline: A deceased man’s friends and coworkers try to come up with the best way to mourn him and comfort his widow, even though it seems like she doesn’t need it.

title: Paper Losses
author: Lorrie Moore
logline: When a former anti-war nudist files for divorce from his hippie-turned-middle-aged conservative wife, a figurative nuclear war fires up between the two suburban parents.

title: To See You Again
author: Alice Adams
logline: A professor in an unhappy marriage obsesses over and fantasizes about a much younger student, imagining how he will age.

title: The Middle Drawer
author: Hortense Calisher
logline: A woman cleans out her dead mother's drawer while she reflects on her mother's life and their relationship.

title: Marching Through Boston
author: John Updike
logline: When a man's wife gets swept up in the Civil Rights movement in the 1960s, he agrees to tag along on a march in Boston while sick in order to save their shaky marriage.

title: Home
author: James Robison
logline: A middle-aged man and his wife struggle to keep up with their teenage daughter who they just adopted six months ago, especially when she takes interest in a boy her age.

title: Ice
author: Elizabeth Tallent
logline: An ice skater in the entertainment industry, to the chagrin of her cat-obsessed mother, performs the same routine each night with a man dressed in a bear suit.

title: Welcome Home
author: Elizabeth Parsons
logline: After a visit to the tropics, a woman returns to her husband and New England home. She struggles with the transition back to her regular life after she realizes that she felt happier and more at home in the tropics.

title: All Ahead Of Them
author: Tobias Wolff
logline: Six days after getting married, a man discovers that his wife has stolen money from their family and friends, leading him to reflect on many other strange behaviors of hers. He ultimately decides that he will stay and spend his life taking the blame for her and smoothing over her mistakes.

title: The King of Sentences
author: Jonathan Lethem
logline: A young couple obsessed with syntax sets off to meet their favorite author.

title: The Ability to Cry
author: Yiyun Li
logline: A young Chinese-American woman struggles to tell her dying father that her son has committed suicide.

title: It Never Happened
author: Emily Hahn
logline: A Portuguese girl in Hong-Kong finds her circumstances suddenly changed with the onset of the Sino-Japanese War, and struggles to find her way out of China despite the ubiquitous presence of the Japanese officers and spiteful former lovers.

title: Playing with Dynamite
author: John Updike
logline: When his wife accuses him of something he can't remember, a man must confront the memories that still linger in his mind.

title: The Tiger
author: Frederick Buechner
logline: A man dresses up as a tiger mascot for a football game, but, as the night progresses, he realizes the tiger has lost its meaning in society.

title: Don't Scrub Off These Names
author: John McNulty
logline: A patient landlady and her peculiar tenant share a curious financial relationship, resulting in an act of generosity that spells freedom for one and ruin for the other.

title: The Bulgarian Poetess
author: John Updike
logline: An American writer travels to Sophia where he meets a famous poetess. He falls in love with her and her attitude.

title: Green Grass, Blue Sky, White House
author: Wright Morris
logline: An investigator stays in a family home in order to become acquainted with the family and all their intricacies while he investigates the case of family's adult son, who has threatens to kill the president of the United States to spare the lives of those involved in Vietnam.

title: Thorofare
author: Susan Minot
logline: In 1980s Boston, a woman and her family finally collect her mother's ashes almost two years after her death. Despite her father's remarriage and her many siblings' variegated lives, they all come together for a touching tribute to their matriarch's memory.

title: The Bulgarian Poetess
author: John Updike
logline: An American writer travels to Sophia where he meets a famous poetess. He falls in love with her and her attitude.

title: The Falls
author: George Saunders
logline: A middle-aged man ruminating on his past failures witnesses a canoe accident and considers sacrificing himself to save two drowning girls.

title: The Haunting of Hajji Hotak
author: Jamil Jan Kochai
logline: As a surveillance agent watches a Muslim family, he quickly grows from suspicion to attachment. When the father of the family needs help, the agent has to decide between what he is supposed to do and what he wants to do, despite the consequences.

title: Paranoia
author: Shirley Jackson
logline: Mr. Beresford falls into a fit of paranoia one day on his way home from work. Mr. Beresford encounters a man in a light hat who he believes is conspiring to hurt him, and who is enlisting others on the street and even Mr. Beresford's wife to help.

title: The Empties
author: Jess Row
logline: In a post-apocalyptic Vermont of the near-future, a former writer picks up her old craft once more in an attempt to document the before and after of her resource-starved, disease-plagued world.

title: Cowboy
author: Thomas McGuane
logline: When an ex-prisoner-turned-cowboy becomes a farmhand, he forms unconventional relationships with the elderly brother and sister who own the ranch.

title: The Secret Goldfish
author: David Means
logline: In Michigan, a young boy whose parents are going through a divorce spends his days fantasizing about his goldfish, Fish.

title: The Wind
author: Lauren Groff
logline: In a rural town, a woman attempts to run away, with her three children, from her abusive husband. While the feat seems straightforward at first, a series of complications causes their escape to become increasingly precarious.

title: Evening and Morning Prayer
author: John Mayo Goss

title: Sculpture I
author: Angela Patrinos
logline: After barely graduating high school, a woman takes a nude modeling job in New York City. Almost without realizing, she forges a strange connection with one of the students, a middle-aged Pakistani man, and their experiences harmonize in unexpected ways.

title: The Other Place
author: Mary Gaitskill
logline: A quasi-reformed stalker worries about the influence of his creepy behaviors on his son.

title: Nero
author: Louise Erdrich
logline: A young girl living with her grandparents is spectator to the conflicts between the members of their restaurant family—including their vicious guard dog, to who she forms an attachment.

title: Willing
author: Lorrie Moore
logline: In the 1990s, a Hollywood star moves back to her hometown of Chicago and tries to find meaning in a relationship with a man whom she does not love.

title: Kilifi Creek
author: Lionel Shriver
logline: A young white girl backpacking through Kenya imposes upon a couple she tangentially knows and has a life-changing near-death experience.

title: The Bookseller
author: Elizabeth Hardwick
logline: Passive and easily satisfied, Roger spends his days managing his secondhand bookstore The Pleiade. He worships modernist classics without fully reading them, he’s gregarious but seldom invited to dinner, and he types novel after novel methodically, but all are rejected. He passes seasons of love and loss in unfailing, impassive routine.

title: The Disaster Stamps of Pluto
author: Louise Erdrich
logline: One of the last inhabitants of a dying midwest town reconsiders the dramatic events and personal tragedies that defined both her and the town’s past after an old friend brings new information to light.

title: Likes
author: Sarah Shun-Lien Bynum
logline: A father struggles to connect with his twelve-year-old daughter who is plagued by self-doubt and isolation, enraptured by social media, and debilitated by tendonitis. Despite her detachment, his daughter may be the only one who can save him from his post-election disillusionment with the country's failures.

title: Corrie
author: Alice Munro
logline: A young heiress in the 1950s takes up a decades-long affair with a married architect, which seems like a safe venture until a mutual friend begins blackmailing them.

title: Quarantine
author: Alix Ohlin
logline: As two friends, Bridget and Angela, grow older, their paths cross and diverge at pivotal moments in their lives while they both deal with the stress of family and marriage.

title: Old Friends
author: Thomas McGuane
logline: Two former Yale roommates, now middle-aged divorced men, reunite in Montana when one of them is being investigated for embezzlement. During the brief time they spend together, the other friend wonders why the clearly unsuitable friendship has gone on for so long.

title: The Trusty
author: Ron Rash
logline: Sinkler escapes from his chain gang with a woman who also wants to escape her own version of prison, however, his escape ends in tragedy.

title: Winky
author: George Saunders
logline: A middle-aged man attends a self-help seminar in hopes of finding the resolve to confront his quirky and off-putting sister and ask her to move out of his home.

title: The Sun, the Moon, the Stars
author: Junot Díaz
logline: A young Dominican-American man struggles to make things better with his girlfriend after she finds out he cheated on her. Throughout their ill-fated vacation to the Dominican Republic, he clings on as she further separates herself from him.

title: Axis
author: Alice Munro
logline: In 1950s Canada, two girls see each other for the last time on a bus ride home from college. Over the following summer vacation, their lives change irrevocably due to boyfriends and pregnancy scares.

title: A Sheltered Woman
author: Yiyun Li
logline: A nanny for newborns takes care of a mother with postpartum depression and her child. Against her own rules, she finds herself getting attached to the baby.

title: Marjorie Lemke
author: Sarah Braunstein
logline: Twenty-year-old Marjorie Lemke spends her days cleaning motel rooms, while her infant daughter sleeps in her cart. One day she meets an intriguing couple who are doing an extended stay at the motel, and she begins an affair with the husband.

title: Tom
author: Mary Lavin
logline: A daughter recounts the story of how her parents came from Ireland to Massachusetts, and the regretful sentiments of each parent upon return visits to their hometowns.

title: Another Short Day in La Luz
author: Harriet Doerr
logline: An old woman takes a day trip through the Mexican town of La Luz. After one of her appointments is unexpectedly cancelled, she must find new ways to spend her day.

title: Boxes
author: Raymond Carver
logline: After his unhappy mother announces she will move homes once again, he and his girlfriend visit her one last time.

title: Paper Lantern
author: Stuart Dybek
logline: A scientist reminisces about an old affair while he watches his time-machine lab burn down.

title: Switzerland
author: Nicole Krauss
logline: A young woman reminisces about her friend with whom she lost contact. She thinks of her friend's past and tries to get in touch with her.

title: Fable
author: Charles Yu
logline: Asked by his therapist to tell a fable, a man recounts his unenchanting life as a lawyer married to a depressed, drug-abusing woman, with a disabled son he's struggling to raise. By filling his unremarkable story with sorceresses, magic, and true love, he attempts to romanticize a life he's desperate to escape.

title: Superstition
author: Sarah Braunstein
logline: A teenage boy grapples with the guilt of selling a fake relic on the Internet. As he navigates the consequences, his father and his father’s girlfriend try to make him feel better. After a series of revelations, the boy—in his attempt to free himself—falls headfirst into a different kind of danger.

title: Ripped Off
author: Alice Adams
logline: After her home is burglarized, Deborah makes some startling realizations about herself and her boyfriend.

title: The Lone Pilgrim
author: Laurie Colwin
logline: A book illustrator spends her free time being a house-sitter, imagining what her life might be like if she lived in their houses. When she goes to work for a certain publisher, the connection they find through their work deepens until the two fall in love, but she worries her satisfaction is fleeting.

title: Dogs Go Wolf
author: Lauren Groff
logline: Two young girls trusted their mother to bring them to place where they could have a better life, but now they are stranded on a mid-Atlantic island. Can they keep each other alive?

title: The Royal Plams
author: Matthew Klam
logline: A man tries to reignite the spark in his failing romantic relationship.

title: Lu, Reshaping
author: Madeleine Thien
logline: A businesswoman has her daughter edit her report for the next day because even though she’s eleven, she “excelled at things like that.” In the morning, the business meeting is cancelled because of a sexual assault investigation. The man accused is someone the businesswoman used to sleep with. Thinking of that makes her think of another man she used to sleep with, the numerous affairs she’s had. She “enjoyed the feeling of different lovers, the newness of strangers.” While she’s waiting for the interview, she checks on her daughters. She thinks about how they “were mystified by her English. It was one thing about her that seemed to both entertain and perturb them. They deployed her expressions to taunt her and the world at large. ‘I have eaten more salt than you have eaten rice,’ they shouted at each other, at their dolls, at strangers on the street.” Her affair with the guy who’s being investigated had lasted three months. “[T]hey agreed…on the importance of seeking out risk and pleasure, and the joy of a temporary room with its own evolving rules.” She thinks about the other man she used to sleep with, how “[h]e was the lover she never would have turned away from.” But this guy, the guy who was her superior in the company, it seems she was not the only one who slept with him. Some of her female co-workers seemed affected by him too. And yet, he’d vouched for the businesswoman, even before their “brief affair, John had lauded her. He had argued for her to be further promoted, which would have meant a better salary, an easing of financial burdens, a three-bedroom apartment for the family, but she had been left to twist in the same position for ten years. Despite her tireless efforts, Lu had stayed near the bottom of the ladder.” The investigator tries to get her to blame the guy, but the businesswoman wonders, “Who was it who demanded shame? Fourteen years at the company. Where had all that time gone? Was John Sadler responsible for that?” She decides not to divulge anything. The man who’s being investigated calls her to apologize. She wonders what it means to be a mother, to be responsible for others when you want to be free. She looks at the questionnaire the investigator gave her. She tries to figure out how to answer it. Starts by writing, “I saw other woman grieving,” deletes that and then writes, “I never grieved.” She then writes in Cantonese, tries to answer why she had an affair. She thinks about having her daughter answer the questionnaire for her, but figures “[i]t was out of the question to ask the child. Was this something, after all, that a mother should do?” She ultimately writes, “Two people had an affair. Nothing more. But also nothing less.” The man who’s being investigated gets hospitalized. Nobody knows why. “Some people in the company pitied him, others didn’t.” His position gets filled by someone else. Life goes on. The businesswoman wants to tell her daughters that, that “[y]ou wanted to change [life] but it changed you, remodelled you for every age. One day, you were an immigrant, loaded down with inexplicable shame; the next you were middle-aged, a mother, and all the risks you’d taken—to live freely, to not be subdued—also made you feel ashamed, as if you’d done nothing but kick the tangerines around.” She realizes she may never understand how the world works. “She’d eaten from the bowl and turned it over; she had been unfaithful and yet faithful, wrong and yet right, lonely and yet beloved, and that was the bitter, that was the sweet quandry of it all.”

title: Aphrodisiac
author: Ruth Prawer Jhabvala
logline: A Cambridge-educated writer returns to India for his brother's wedding only to develop feelings for his brother's new wife.

title: Kid MacArthur
author: Stephanie Vaughn
logline: A sister remains a faithful friend to her brother as he navigates the strict parenting of their military father, spending his youth fighting in Vietnam, and his return home after the war as a changed man living apart from his family and forging his own path in life for the first time.

title: The Science of Flight
author: Yiyun Li
logline: A Chinese American woman living in contemporary Wisconsin plans out a vacation to England rather China, her usual destination. The thought of abandoning her home country takes her back to the more difficult moments of her life, from her estrangement from her parents to her failed marriage.

title: A Country Love Story
author: Jean Stafford
logline: During a Northeastern winter in their new isolated country home, a woman slowly succumbs to the gaslighting and manipulation of her husband.

title: Coach
author: Mary Robinson
logline: A family begins a new life in a college town where the father will coach the college's JV football team.

title: Three Thousand Dollars
author: David Lipsky
logline: When a young college student's father gives him money for tuition, the student spends it away and lies to his mother for money. His father catches him, but the student remains unsure if his mother knows the truth.

title: The Swastika On Our Door
author: Alice Adams
logline: A hidden photograph reveals a story about the strained fraternal relations between two brothers spanning decades in mid-twentieth century America.

title: The Breeze
author: Joshua Ferris
logline: A New Yorker tired of the cold seeks to make the most of the year’s first spring breeze with her resistant husband.

title: The Night of the Satellite
author: T.C. Boyle
logline: A couple in grad school who witness a domestic dispute have opposing views on whether to intervene, which leads to tumultuous arguments in their own relationship as well.

title: Real Estate, Real Estate
author: Lorrie Moore
logline: Terrence and Ruth, a middle-aged couple, move house for a fresh start - but their new house is in disrepair. Ruth contends with sickness, unfulfillment, and her staling marriage while laboriously cleaning it.

title: Leg
author: Steven Polansky
logline: Father and parishioner Dave Long sustains a leg injury in a softball game and refuses to have it treated. As his leg worsens, his rocky relationship with his son begins to heal.

title: Dede
author: Mavis Gallant
logline: A beloved yet dim-witted uncle averts disaster when a wasp attack interrupts a mundane luncheon party in the bourgeois home of a Parisian magistrate.

title: The Bell Ringer
author: John Burnside
logline: A woman, lonely in her marriage, judges the adulterous actions of her sister-in-law, only to discover the two of them are not so different after all.

title: A Beneficiary
author: Nadine Gordimer
logline: The daughter of a recently-deceased actress discovers that the man she thinks is her father may not be—and that she might actually be the offspring of a highly acclaimed actor who just so happens to be in town.

title: In Greenwich There Are Many Gravelled Walks
author: Hortense Calisher
logline: Fresh out of a stint in the army, a young journalism student confronts suicide, isolation, and dilettantism as he drives his alcoholic mother from New York to Connecticut.

title: The High Divide
author: Charles D'Ambrosio
logline: Ignatius, a young orphan, develops an unlikely friendship with his bully, Donny, and Donny's father.

title: The Five-Forty-Eight
author: John Cheever
logline: A Manhattan businessman is stalked by his former secretary and one-night stand on a train ride home.

title: Surrounded by Sleep
author: Akhil Sharma
logline: A young boy deals with difficult life changes one fateful year after his high-achieving brother nearly drowns in a swimming pool and falls into a coma.

title: The Dressmaker's Child
author: William Trevor
logline: On the way home from an unexpected outing, a young auto-mechanic accidentally hits a little girl — he keeps driving. No one knows he did this, but from then on he must grapple with his own guilt and the girl's mother.

title: Tide Pools
author: Alice Adams
logline: Judith, a professor of marine biology, takes a sabbatical year after her childhood friend drunkenly calls her on her birthday

title: Northeast Regional
author: Emma Cline
logline: A bitter divorcee and distant father having an affair with a younger, married woman gets a call that his son has gotten into trouble at boarding school. He travels to the school, where the headmaster says his son, who beat up another student, must transfer. In a series of events that makes him increasingly bitter, he ends up making his son's girlfriend cry in a restaurant.

title: Color and Light
author: Sally Rooney
logline: A solitary young hotel clerk finds himself enticed by a mysterious, sophisticated writer. Both desire intimacy, but find their romance obstructed by unspeakable kinds of loneliness.

title: Seeing Ershadi
author: Nicole Krauss
logline: A dancer becomes disillusioned after moving to Tel Aviv to study under a long admired choreographer. Once she begins to see an actor's face at pivotal points in her life, she decides to quit the dance company and leave Tel Aviv.

title: In the Gloaming
author: Alice Elliott Dark
logline: In the 1990s, as a mother watches her thirty-three-year old son slowly die from AIDS, she grows closer to him than she ever has before.

title: A Love Story
author: Samantha Hunt
logline: After kicking her husband out and changing the locks, a mother imagines he is still living with her, distant and uninterested in sex. Lying in bed, she conjures up old memories and imagines new ones, grappling with questions of selfhood, identity, womanhood, and motherhood. One night, her real husband returns, and she lets him back in.

title: A Summer Day
author: Jean Stafford
logline: A boy comes to live at an Indian reservation after being orphaned when his grandmother dies.

title: The Trouble of Marcie Flint
author: John Cheever
logline: A family man tries to unpack how a seemingly perfect day ended with his children poisoned and himself newly divorced as he flees to Italy on a ship.

title: The Burglar
author: Sarah Shun-Lien Bynum
logline: A would-be burglar enters a suburban home. In the same town, a woman drives home for an exterminator appointment, and her husband tries to write the season premiere of a time-traveling crime show.

title: The Prairie Wife
author: Curtis Sittenfeld
logline: A young woman jaded about her quiet suburban life obsessively follows a famous closeted rural food blogger, with whom she was in a secretive homosexual relationship when they were teenagers.

title: The Cryptozoologist
author: Tony Earley
logline: Amid a manhunt in her town for a bombing suspect, a widow becomes obsessed with finding Bigfoot.

title: The Polish Rider
author: Ben Lerner
logline: An artist in New York City accidentally leaves two of her paintings in an Uber, then sets out with an old friend to find them—but the odds of recovery aren’t good.

title: The Afterlife
author: John Updike
logline: A middle aged friend group take a drive to the beach.

title: The Girl Who Sang With The Beatles
author: Robert Hemenway
logline: An unsatisfied married couple watches their relationship become more strained until the wife begins to fantasize about singing with the Beatles.

title: An Honest Woman
author: Ottessa Moshfegh
logline: In a contemporary rural American town, a psychopathic 60-year-old man strikes up a deceitful relationship with his young female neighbor.

title: The Good Samaritan
author: Thomas McGuane
logline: After an injury that temporarily prohibits a divorced rancher from working, he frequently visits his imprisoned son, leaving his new ranchhand to develop a curious relationship with his elderly mom.

title: The Headstrong Historian
author: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie
logline: A southern Nigerian woman lives through the colonial invasion of white Europeans, losing her son to assimilation and indoctrination that leads him to view her and her culture as savages. Decades later, her granddaughter, a historian, seeks to reclaim her past.

title: Miracle Polish
author: Steven Millhauser
logline: A dissatisfied man buys "miracle" mirror polish from a mysterious stranger and becomes obsessed with how the polish changes his reflection and that of his lover.

title: Their Losses
author: Peter Taylor
logline: Three women from a small town, each with their respective ideas about grief and loss, meet for breakfast on a train.

title: Boys Town
author: Jim Shepard
logline: A 39-year-old war veteran returns to live with his mother after his wife kicks him out for domestic abuse. Suffering from what his mother believes is PTSD, the man becomes increasingly anxious and bitter. When the cops come looking for him for one of an assorted range of former crimes, a string of events ends with him shooting at the house of his grocery-store crush and running into the woods.

title: Ba Baboon
author: Thomas Pierce
logline: A woman and her brother are hiding from two violent dogs in the pantry in a house they broke in to, and she regrets bringing him into this because he has not fully recovered from his traumatic head injury.

title: Yurt
author: Sarah Shun-Lien Bynum
logline: When her co-worker returns pregnant and happy from a year of travel, a seventh grade English teacher reflects on her dissatisfaction with her own life and her longing for decisiveness.

title: Katania
author: Lara Vapnyar
logline: Two little girls form a tumultuous friendship that impacts each of their life's dreams and desires in deep, unconscious ways—a fact that only becomes evident when they reconnect many years down the line.

title: Influenza
author: Daniel Menaker
logline: A teacher at a private school in 1970s New York begins to see a psychoanalyst several times a week because he struggles with awkwardness and timidity in social settings. The analyst encourages the man to pursue a wealthy widow whose children attend his school.

title: The Nightingales Sing
author: Elizabeth Parsons
logline: A young woman from a strict household heads off to a countryside home with an older man where she falls for the freedom of being out late at night, being romanced. However, she is forced to return home the real fun begins, dreaming of what the night could have been instead.

title: Omakase
author: Weike Wang
logline: A couple who met online eventually move in together in New York City, but overtime, their relationship completely falls apart.

title: The Iceman
author: Emma Cline
logline:
A young man is working at a hotel resort during
quarantine-era Covid. When a quirky couple comes to stay, his service to them makes him reconsider why he’s making the lifestyle choices he is and what the point is of self-restraint.

title: Further Tales About Men and Women
author: William Maxwell
logline: In a series of commentaries on the human condition — life, truth, happiness, death — a spinster sister takes in her dead sister’s children; a man is entranced by the endless waves which roll and crash in the ocean; a carpenter wrestles with the burden of being everyone’s confidante; a dying railroad crossing watchman shares a simple but complex wisdom.

title: Blue Spruce
author: David Long
logline: After a man's suicide, his former wife and sister live together. at odds with one another as they differently processes their feelings of grief.

title: Every Night for a Thousand Years
author: Chris Adrian
logline: During the Civil War, a young man finds purpose helping the wounded while visiting his own injured brother.

title: Sur: A Summary Report of the Yelcho Expedition to the Antarctic, 1909-1910
author: Ursula K. Le Guin
logline: An all-female expeditionary crew endeavor to become the first humans to reach the South Pole.

title: Sarah
author: Allegra Goodman
logline: A middle-aged writer-turned-community center professor finds her already scarce writing time in jeopardy when her husband’s mother suffers a drug overdose.

title: A Man Like Him
author: Yiyun Li
logline: In modern-day China, a man previously accused of being a pedophile sets out to meet and provide support for a man whose daughter has publicly accused him of being an adulterer.

title: The Surveyor
author: Henry Roth
logline: In Seville, the Spanish police stop and interrogate a couple on why they left a wreath near a public monument, though the couple refuses to tell the truth.

title: Visitation
author: Brad Watson
logline: A depressed, divorced father visits his son in Southern California, hoping to encounter a bit of joie de vivre, if for only a few days.

title: Safari
author: Jennifer Egan
logline: Lou, a middle-aged record producer, brings his two kids, Rolph (11) and Charlie (14), and his new girlfriend Mindy (23) to a safari run by an old friend in Kenya.

title: It's Cold Out There
author: Perdita Buchan
logline: A couple goes on a trip from Boston to Cape Cod and visit a fortune teller in the process.

title: God's Caravan
author: Tiphanie Yanique
logline: A lonely young boy finds faith through the teachings of a radical new Pastor. The only question is: is he truly a Pastor or merely an imposter?

title: Where I'm Calling From
author: Raymond Carver
logline: Two men recovering from their alcoholism sit on a porch at a "drying out" facility. While one talks about his tumultuous marriage, the other begins to reframe his own wife and love affair.

title: Blueprints for St. Louis
author: Ben Marcus
logline: Two Chicago architects work on a memorial for a bombing in St. Louis as their marriage falls apart.

title: What Can You do with a General
author: Emma Cline
logline: When a man's children return home to visit him and and his wife for Christmas, he reflects on their tense family dynamic, his past aggressive and abusive behavior, and his distance from his eldest daughter, who has found a new family with her boyfriend and his child.

title: Haven
author: Alice Munro
logline: A young girl goes to stay with her uncle and aunt, where she learns that there may be more to their marriage than it initially seems.

title: Bumblebees
author: Bobbie Ann Mason
logline: A college student visits her divorcee mother and her widowed friend on the farm they live on together and together they each start to push through their pasts to brighter futures.

title: Audition
author: Saïd Sayrafiezadeh
logline: In the 1990s, a 19-year-old aspiring actor-turned-construction worker develops an affinity for crack cocaine, making him doubt the promise of his future.

title: Victrola
author: Wright Morris
logline: Bundy, an old man, agrees to take care of Miss Tyler’s dog. However, Bundy is ashamed of the pet, and waits for the canine to die.

title: Deep-Holes
author: Alice Munro
logline: A woman's son experiences a terrifying accident that shifts the trajectory of his life and changes his relationship with his parents and siblings throughout his life.

title: The Warlock
author: Jean Stafford
logline: A woman who suffers from an unknown illness on a cruise is haunted by the ship’s doctor.

title: ID
author: Joyce Carol Oates
logline: A middle-school girl is pulled out of math class to identify a battered corpse that the police believe to be her often absent and unavailable mother.

title: A Summer’s Long Dream
author: Nancy Hale
logline: On a trip to their deceased cousin’s seaside estate, a young woman strains against the constant insults and reprimands leveraged by her demanding elderly mother and aunt.

title: The Conductor
author: Aleksandar Hemon
logline: A young would-be poet develops a complicated relationship with the most famous living Bosnian poet at the time. This relationship ends decades later on another continent when that poet dies, and the young man finds a life of his own that doesn't involve poetry.

title: Cold Little Bird
author: Ben Marcus
logline: A Jewish couple must learn to deal with their 10-year-old son who seems to deeply hate them and harbor anti-semitic views.

title: Breatharians
author: Callan Wink
logline: In a rural American town, a boy must exterminate a horde of cats in his family's barn while his parents' marriage disintegrates around him.

title: Jack, July
author: Victor Lodato
logline: Jack wanders around the world trying to find the right person, but nobody seems to stay long enough—that is, until he meets Jamie, a person he never thought he could love, and things change forever.

title: Are We Not Men?
author: T.C. Boyle
logline: A man from a future overrun by genetic modification struggles in vain to keep unregulated technology out of his neighborhood and marriage.

title: First Dark
author: Elizabeth Spencer
logline: A woman who cares for her ill mother falls in love with a successful man from her hometown, but cannot marry him until her mother’s death.

title: Glimpse Into Another Country
author: Wright Morris
logline: An elderly academic with an anxious wife is enlivened by a trip to New York, where he has an unlikely series of encounters with the peculiar woman who sat beside him on the plane.

title: Friend of My Youth
author: Alice Munro
logline: Following the death of her mother, a daughter recalls her mother gossiping about a small family in the Ottowa valley where a man shamelessly robs two sisters of their inheritance through marriage.

title: Show Don't Tell
author: Curtis Sittenfeld
logline: Ruthie, an experienced writer, reflects on the scholarship opportunity that set her career in motion.

title: From a Farther Room
author: David Gilbert
logline: After partying for the first time in a while with his childhood friend, a middle-aged father in North Carolina must reckon with the scary truth about his hangover.

title: Underground
author: David Gilbert
logline: A newly out and divorced father navigates his familial and sexual relationships while longing for some further purpose in life.

title: The Game
author: Frances Gray Patton
logline: A wealthy woman's ploy to flaunt her wealth is foiled by her old friend's seeming indifference to opulence - until they part, and the friend asks for money. The afternoon is ruined when the woman realizes that her obsession with money has ruined her outlook on life.

title: The Smoker
author: David Schickler
logline: A lonely high school English teacher develops a crush on one of his students, who continually writes him notes about the books she reads and calls him out of the blue. When her family invites him over for dinner to celebrate her admission to Princeton, he is caught off guard when they announce they want him to marry her.

title: He Knew
author: Donald Antrim
logline: A couple, an older man with a young wife, traverse a typical day, dealing with their respective mental health issues atop long-standing marital tensions.

title: What You Pawn I Will Redeem
author: Sherman Alexie
logline: A homeless Native American man goes on a journey to get one thousand dollars in order to buy back his grandma's regalia.

title: The Rug
author: Meg Mullins
logline: When a rug merchant's best customer requests a new rug for her home, but complications arise, he must decide how far he's willing to go for a paycheck.

title: The Intermediate Class
author: Sam Allingham
logline: A second-generation Russian immigrant living in contemporary Michigan finds himself caught up in a sad but emotive group of friends when he takes a continuing education course on Intermediate German.

title: The Ambassador
author: Edward Newhouse
logline: A man who sponsors his cousin’s immigration to America struggles to protect his daughter from the hard truths of his relative’s experience in Nazi concentration camps.

title: In the Middle of the Fields
author: Mary Lavin
logline: A widow in the Irish countryside needs someone to mow her overgrown fields. She hires her neighbor, who visits her house the following night, but a renegotiation of their agreement is not the only thing he's after.

title: The Shape of a Teardrop
author: T.C. Boyle
logline: An adult son is living with his parents when they begin to take stronger measures toward kicking him out. They’ve dropped him from the family phone plan, put a lock on the refrigerator, and now have put an official court-approved eviction notice on his door. His parents aren’t sure what went wrong with him. “He had every advantage. We loved him, we still love him, our only child, who came to us as the sweetest and truest blessing from God when I was forty-one and so empty inside…” The son doesn’t understand what his parents are thinking. How is he supposed to get a job without cell service or a car, which he doesn’t have anymore since his parents won’t loan him the money to take it to the shop? When his mom comes home from work, he storms out with the eviction notice in hand to yell at her, and she thinks about how he doesn’t even remember that it’s her birthday. He asks her, “You want me to die?” and she says, in her anger, “‘Yes,’” and then, “‘If you’re going to die, go ahead and do it—but do it someplace else, will you? Will you at least do that for us?’” She immediately says she doesn’t mean it but he’s already storming away. Now, the son is thinking about his own son, which he had on accident when he was a teenager. He’s not on great terms with the mother, and he thinks his mother resents that he’s made it hard for her to see her grandson. The son tries to find a lawyer to help him sue his parents for breach of contract, that “by virtue of their giving me my own room in the house since I was an infant and freely letting me move back in when I had no place else to go, they had entered into an unwritten contract to provide me with shelter, and that, even if it was within their rights to evict me, they at least had to give me six months’ notice, because you can’t just throw somebody out in the street, unless you’re in some country where they randomly kick down doors and put people in concentration camps.” He loses the case. After a lot of stalling, he moves out, and his son and the mother of his child move into his old room. His new apartment is less than ideal and so are the people he’s hanging around. He no longer talks to his father, but his mother puts him back on the family’s phone plan and now calls him every day. She mainly wants to talk about his son. She wants them to spend more time together. She sends him pictures his son drew in school: "fish in tanks, squirrels and dogs and cars, the usual sort of thing, except for one that said ‘Dad’ on it in big red bleeding letters and showed a kid’s face, his face, obscured by a swarm of floating misshapen blobs that I finally figured out were teardrops, as if he was sending me a message.” He figures his mother or the child’s mother put his son up to it. He thinks “the kid was no artist and you couldn’t really what [the blobs] were supposed to be.”

title: Leaving Maverley
author: Alice Munro
logline: In mid-century, small-town Maverley, a veteran police officer meets a sheltered teenage girl who become rebellious. They remain acquaintances throughout the years, and he follows gossip about her troubled family life.

title: Mother's Day
author: George Saunders
logline: One Mother's Day, two old women reflect on their relationships with their children--present and absent--and with the same adulterous man. When their paths cross at a crucial moment, one woman's refusal to accept the help of her husband's secret lover leads to her death.

title: Getaway
author: Robert M. Coates
logline: A man escapes a hit and run accident and feels immense guilt until he meets his own misfortune.

title: Fogbound in Avalon
author: Elizabeth McGrath
logline: A professor leaves her job and her husband for her ancestral home of Newfoundland. There, she confronts depression, isolation, old friends, and old love.

title: Celtic Twilight
author: Joanna Ostrow
logline: When a Master's student in anthropology researches the Highlands of Scotland with his hunting dog by his side, he encounters an elderly couple who teach him about the local culture and traditions.

title: Nothing to Ask For
author: Dennis McFarland
logline: As he naviagtes his own sobriety, a man finds out that his best friend of twenty years has two months to live due to HIV/AIDS. With help from the dying friend's lover, the man helps prepare his friend for a final bronchoscopy.

title: Valentine
author: Tessa Hadley
logline: A teenage girl in 1970s England falls in love with a boy who introduces her to Samuel Beckett and Bob Dylan. What starts off as an innocent relationship, however, turns into something that neither of them will ever be able to erase.

title: The Women
author: William Trevor
logline: A motherless young girl sent to boarding school by her single father is rattled by two women who begin to appear in her life in strange ways.

title: Cat Person
author: Kristen Roupenian
logline: A college sophomore meets a thirty-something-year-old guy while working. Despite being exciting initially, the relationship heads towards uncomfortable territory.

title: The Bog Girl
author: Karen Russell
logline: A teenage boy falls in love with a two-thousand-year-old girl that he discovers preserved in a nearby bog. But not everyone approves of their blossoming relationship, especially not the boy's mother.

title: Waugh
author: Bryan Washington
logline: In downtown Houston, a teenage boy hustles for an older pimp and navigates an increasingly intimate relationship with one of his clients. He also keeps the pimp’s HIV diagnosis a secret from the rest of their crew.

title: A Day on Ragged
author: Donald Hall
logline: A grandfather renews the family tradition of blueberry-picking on Ragged Mountain with his grandson, showing him secret landmarks of family legacy on the way.

title: Dirty Words
author: Antonya Nelson
logline: A woman married to a much older man feels miserable during pregnancy, having abandoned frequent alcohol consumption, insecure about her husband's obsession with his ex-wife, a dead political poet, and missing her carefree youth. When she finally gives birth, she begins to see her aging husband as disgusting and infant-like and begins to contemplate divorce.

title: Community Life
author: Lorrie Moore
logline: A young librarian with two dead parents moves across the country and meets an idealistic but shallow man. When their relationship falls apart, he urges her to give more of herself to the community, ignorant of the ways in which she's had to give so much away already.

title: The Unborn Ghosts
author: Nancy Cardozo
logline: Caught up in memories of the past, a woman remembers a fateful summer dinner party at the start of World War II that left her family more divided than ever.

title: Some Women
author: Alice Munro
logline: When a young girl gets a job as a caretaker for a wealthier middle-aged man, she finds herself in the middle of social tensions between his mother-in-law, his wife, and the flirtatious masseuse.

title: Free Radicals
author: Alice Munro
logline: A recently widowed woman lets a man into her house to look at her fuse box — but soon realizes that the man did not come for the fuse box at all.

title: The Underground Gardens
author: T.C. Boyle
logline: A determined immigrant man decides to win over a woman by doing what he does best — digging her an underground mansion.

title: Act of Faith
author: Irwin Shaw
logline: A Jewish soldier receives a letter from his father in America which details his experiences with Anti-Semitism, and causes him to reflect on his own life. He realizes that his friends have not faced the discrimination he has, but is glad when they acknowledge this and treat him the way they always have — as an equal.

title: Death of a Favorite
author: J. F. Powers
logline: A bitter rivalry between two priests and a cat takes a violent turn as the two men orchestrate the death of the animal - but the unexpected and miraculous consequence of their plot leave them horrified.

title: Motherlode
author: Thomas McGuane
logline: When a young man in Oklahoma on a cattle genetics job is threatened by a conman with a gun, he gets wrapped up into an exciting drug scheme that suddenly makes his life before seem incredibly dull.

title: Shape-ups at Delilah’s
author: Rion Amilcar Scott
logline: In Cross River, there's only one place to get a hair cut and that's at Delilah's--the first shop to be run by  lady barber Tiny who is rumored to be using magic on her clients.

title: The Love of My Life
author: T.C. Boyle
logline: Freshly graduated from high school, a young couple must decide how to handle an unwanted pregnancy and their crippling sense of shame.

title: My Blithe, Sad Bird
author: Jean Stafford
logline: After seeing a familiar name in the phone book, a woman decides to visit the house where she studied abroad years before.

title: Selection Week
author: Hurmat Kazmi
logline: As a young gay Pakistani man goes through the interview process to become an Air Force officer, he reflects on how he got there and why he might want to be chosen after all. A crush on a fellow interviewee both complicates things and makes them simpler, in turns.

title: A Voice in the Night
author: Steven Millhauser
logline: A young Jewish boy wavers between his father’s militant atheism and his anxious desires to speak to God, only to become an old man still asking the same questions of his faith.

title: The Relive Box
author: T.C. Boyle
logline: In a contemporary home in Southern California, a box that allows people to relive past moments of their lives complicates an already-strained father-daughter relationship.

title: Nobody's Business
author: Jhumpa Lahiri
logline: Miranda, a twenty-two year old white woman living in Boston, begins an affair with Dev, a married Bengali man. Meanwhile, Miranda's co-worker Laxmi complains about her cousin's husband, who recently fell in love with a British stranger.

title: Run, Run, Run, Run
author: A. J. Liebling
logline: In England during World War II, a literary critic turned war correspondent finds himself face to face with his own mortality on an air raid mission.

title: The Dark Arts
author: Ben Marcus
logline: An American in Germany stays at a men's hostel while undergoing expensive medical treatment and falls into despair as he waits for his despondent girlfriend to arrive.

title: Blind Jozef Pronek
author: Aleksandar Hemon
logline: A Bosnian journalist visits America during the Bosnian ethnic cleansing and moves into a dirty Chicago apartment with a woman he once met and her on-and-off boyfriend. He takes on a series of humiliating jobs and tries to avoid thinking about the unknown fate of his parents.

title: Nachman from Los Angeles
author: Leonard Michaels
logline: A graduate student finds himself embroiled in a strange sort of psychological game after he agrees to write a paper for another well-off student.

title: Beautiful Girl
author: Alice Adams
logline: When Ardis Bascombe drunkenly kissed Walpole Greene one college night, she did not know she would be stirring a deadly attraction that might be fatal for her.

title: Companion
author: Sana Krasikov
logline: A Russian-American divorcee with a strange living situation tries to navigate her complicated relationships—with friends, roommates, and lovers.

title: Pigeon Feathers
author: John Updike
logline: When a fourteen-year-old boy moves with his family to a farm town, he reads a book that leads him to have a crisis of faith and he begins to question what really happens after death.

title: The Valetudinarian
author: Joshua Ferris
logline: On his sixty-sixth birthday, a cranky hypochondriac widower orders a pizza to his Florida condo. Instead, he gets a prostitute — and a heart attack.

title: Helping
author: Robert Stone
logline: A counselor breaks his sobriety streak after several meetings with a frustrating client. After arguing with his wife while drunk, the counselor begins to feel murderous and must fight his violent urges to earn back her trust.

title: Naima
author: Hisham Matar
logline: A young boy lives with his parents, former Libyan aristocrats exiles, in Cairo. Before, during, and after his mother's death he finds comfort in Naima, the family's maid with whom he shares a closer relationship than he does with his parents.

title: The House Behind a Weeping Cherry
author: Ha Jin
logline: A Chinese-American sweatshop worker in New York City falls in love with a prostitute and urges her to quit sex work. The couple must figure out how to escape their former lives and financial debts.

title: The Black Room
author: John Updike
logline: A son takes his aging mother back on a visit to his childhood home. Though he expected the house to remain at least a little bit familiar, both his fromer home and his mother had changed considerably with the passing of time.

title: Xuela
author: Jamaica Kincaid
logline: A young, African-Carib girl is raised by the woman who does her father's laundry after her mother dies in childbirth. Feeling a lack of love in her life, the girl seeks to understand her relationship with her distant father and dead mother.

title: Three Players of A Summer Game
author: Tennessee Williams
logline: Set in Mississippi, a second generation planter leaves his wife for a recent widower and her 12-year-old daughter. His actions driven by alcoholism, however, threaten to spoil his affair.

title: The Bad Graft
author: Karen Russell
logline: A young couple in their 20s set off on a spontaneous trip to the American West that leads them to Joshua Tree, where the girl is possessed by the spirit of a tree, forcing the couple to renegotiate their impulsive relationship.

title: The Waiting
author: James Agee
logline: After a young woman in Tennessee hears that her husband has been in a serious automobile accident, she waits with her aunt as her brother goes out to determine the severity.

title: Escape from Spiderhead
author: George Saunders
logline: In a lab nicknamed "Spiderhead," experiments involving mind-altering drugs are run on convicted murderers. After he sleeps with two female prisoners, a male prisoner is forced to decide which woman he would like to give a pain-inducing drug.

title: The Third and Final Continent
author: Jhumpa Lahiri
logline: An Indian-American immigrant recalls his life's journey, which goes from Calcutta to Boston. In Boston he rented a room from a strange old woman and fell in love with his wife long after their arranged marriage.

title: In Roseau
author: Jamaica Kincaid
logline: A young woman sent to board with an older couple claims bodily autonomy and control over her own fate.

title: The Future
author: Joseph McElroy
logline: Ann and her son Davey witness a hold-up at their favorite French restaurant.

title: The Slightest Distance
author: Henry Bromell
logline: A mother and her three boys are on a small Greek island, where they prepare to reunite with her husband. Before they leave, they attend a party, and spend time reflecting on the possibility that they may never see their missing loved one again.

title: Beatrice Trueblood's Story
author: Jean Stafford
logline: A woman with an aversion to yelling regrets her wish to be deaf so that she does not need to marry her fiance who is being argumentative.

title: Herman Melville, Volume I
author: Victor Lodato
logline: After her father kills himself, a young girl runs away with a traveling, unhoused stranger she meets at the bus stop. The two scrape and save for a life together until one day, she wakes up and he's gone. After looking for him in the cold, surviving an assault, and accepting help from a stranger, the girl realizes he's betrayed her, taking their savings and leaving. The next year, she gives birth to their child.

title: Not Another Word
author: Richard Thurman
logline: Two boys become friends after one of them displays unflinching honesty in the face of a tyrannical teacher. Ultimately, their friendship is destroyed when the same honesty robs the second boy of some of his childhood ignorance.

title: The Point
author: Charles D'Ambrosio
logline: A young man from The Point, has been given the role of escorting older drunk party guests back to their houses.

title: What is Remembered
author: Alice Munro
logline: After a funeral, a married woman accepts a ride from a stranger. As the day progresses, it becomes clear that there is attraction between the two of them.
