title: Funny Little Snake
author: Tessa Hadley
logline: After her husband's ex-wife's 9-year-old daughter visits, a woman is eager to return the girl and have time alone again. However, when she drops the girl off, she is appalled by the state of the girl's home and moved by the girl's desire to go back with her. The next day, she takes the child back in secret.

title: What We Talk About When We Talk About Anne Frank
author: Nathan Englander
logline: When a middle-aged man is visited by his wife’s two orthodox friends from Jerusalem, the husband finds his secular Jewish lifestyle in South Florida under attack. To clear the air between them, the two couples smoke weed.

title: Screenwriter
author: Charles D'Ambrosio
logline: A bipolar screenwriter in a New York City psych ward falls in love with a depressed Yugoslavian ballerina.

title: Bech Takes Pot Luck
author: John Updike
logline: A writer summers with his mistress and part of her family. The group runs into one of his former students, and they all smoke together.

title: The Pugilist at Rest
author: Thom Jones
logline: A teenage Marine recruit befriends another recruit who dreams of becoming a a New York City artist. Together, they fight in the Vietnam War: he develops epilepsy, and his friend dies.

title: White Angel
author: Michael Cunningham
logline: A nine-year-old who idolizes his older brother plans to move to Woodstock with him one day. For the time being, however, they are stuck in Cleveland, where they dabble in drugs, sex, and alcohol before his older brother's untimely demise.

title: Wildwood
author: Junot Díaz
logline: In New Jersey, a punk-obsessed Dominican teenager deals with a tumultuous relationship with her mother, who has been diagnosed with breast cancer. At a breaking point, she runs away from home.

title: Face
author: Alice Munro
logline: A man with a large birthmark on his face reflects on his life and the neighbor girl he used to know as he cleans up the garden of his family home years after his parents have passed away.

title: The Nemesis
author: Jean Stafford
logline: The friendship between two college students is based entirely on dislike and desperation - but also need. One has an eating disorder that she needs help overcoming, while the other desperately wants access to luxury and wealth. As they grow closer, secrets and lies threaten to ruin their relationship.

title: How You Play the Game
author: Paul Tyner
logline: A good-hearted cop obsessed with the game of pool is exposed as a thrill-seeker who loves abusing the power that comes with his job

title: Your Place is Empty
author: Anne Tyler
logline: An Iranian mother makes an extended visit to her son in America and struggles to fit in with his new family and adjust to their foreign way of life.

title: For Esmé-With Love and Squalor
author: J.D. Salinger
logline: Upon hearing about an upcoming wedding, a former American soldier reminisces about the time he met a young girl who gave him the recourse to survive the war.

title: Sur
author: Ursula K. Le Guin
logline: A woman shares her unpublished account of leading an all-woman expedition to the South Pole from Chile years before the first expedition arrived in 1912.

title: Revival Road
author: Louise Erdrich
logline: A woman who lives peacefully in the country spends most of her time with an artist who lives nearby, invested in his life and work. When the artist faces troubles due to a clumsy and destructive teenage boy, the woman must confront her feelings for the man.

title: The Way People Run
author: Christopher Tilghman
logline: A man leaves his family in NYC to look for a job out West. During the trip, he helps an injured young boy, sleeps with a waitress, and considers leaving his family for good.

title: Bronze
author: Jeffrey Eugenides
logline: A college freshman, Eugene, has been struggling with his identity since he was assaulted by an older man at aged fourteen. After an evening of partying in New York, Eugene meets a gay man named Kent on the train and decides to take ownership of himself and his body.

title: The Way We Live Now
author: Susan Sontag
logline: When a man living in New York in the 1980s contracts HIV/AIDS, his friends constantly visit him in the hospital, leading to tears, drama, and questions of mortality and survival.

title: In An Early Winter
author: Roger Angell
logline: A young woman marries her perfect husband after two months of dating. However, once they're married she learns about disturbing accidents in her husband's past and fears he isn't what he seems.

title: Winter Barley
author: Andrea Lee
logline: An elderly man and a young woman couple learn about each other and themselves at a remote estate in Scotland.

title: Javi
author: Han Ong
logline: An undocumented teenaged live-in helper and an eccentric elderly painter form an unlikely relationship in the southern U.S. borderlands.

title: What Kind of Furniture Would Jesus Pick?
author: Annie Proulx
logline: In 1999, a Wyoming ranch owner estranged from his ex-wife, sons, and grandchildren deliberates over what to do with his property when he dies.

title: Save the Reaper
author: Alice Munro
logline: A woman allows her grandchildren's road trip games in the Canadian backcountry. Distracted by her own nostalgia, she unwittingly takes them to a strange, unfamiliar house.

title: A Sandstone Farmhouse
author: John Updike
logline: After his mother passes, a middle-aged man reminisces on the relationship between himself, his mother, and their house in rural Pennsylvania.

title: Peking Duck
author: Ling Ma
logline: A daughter and a mother wonder what the lesson of their story is.

title: Ship Island
author: Elizabeth Spencer
logline: A teenage girl is swept into the wealthy side of her coastal town by her new boyfriend, but soon finds that she longs for adventure and freedom outside of his superficial social scene.

title: The Yellow Beret
author: Mary Lavin
logline: After reading about two murders in the paper, a mother panics because her son has been missing since that morning.

title: A Rich Man
author: Edward P. Jones
logline: Stuck in a loveless marriage for over forty years, a retired couple moves into a senior living apartment with the renewed promise to work on their marriage. When the opposite turns out to be true, the elderly husband attempts to find new love with a much younger woman who isn't what she seems.

title: Tenth of December
author: George Saunders
logline: An imaginative, bullied young boy and an elderly, suicidal cancer patient save each other from freezing to death one day in December.

title: The Guns in the Closet
author: Jose Yglesias
logline: A middle-aged couple hides guns in their house for their revolutionary son.

title: A Gift From the City
author: John Updike
logline: When an impoverished man shows up to a wealthy woman's door in dire need of help, she gives him ten dollars and tries to send him on his way. The man insists that he return the next day to thank her husband for the money, but she isn't quite sure if things are as they seem.

title: A Spoiled Man
author: Daniyal Mueenuddin
logline: A destitute Pakistani man asks to work for a wealthy family in modern-day Pakistan. When he loses something that he values most, the man finally learns the brutal reality of his position in society.

title: On The Lake
author: Ellen Douglas
logline: A mother invites a former employee to join her on a boat ride where everything takes a turn for the worse.

title: The Bella Lingua
author: John Cheever
logline: An American expat who lives in Rome struggles to understand his adopted country, especially the Italian language. When he finally finds the right teacher, he is overjoyed, but her unique personal life quickly pervades their lessons and confounds their rapport.

title: The Thing in the Forest
author: A. S. Byatt
logline:
A World War II era fairytale-like story of two young evacuees who witness a strange event in childhood, and are reunited in adulthood by a long serious of unlikely coincidences.
During World War II, two young evacuees witness a strange event in their childhood. This event leaves a strong impression on both girls, and it proceeds to shape their futures into a long series of unlikely coincidences.

title: Meneseteung
author: Alice Munro
logline: Drawing from Almeda Roth’s 1873 poetry collection Offerings and Roth’s town newspaper the Vidette, an unnamed researcher guides the reader through a rich biography of Roth’s personal affairs, love interest, and ultimate death.

title: Great Barrier Reef
author: Diane Johnson
logline: A bitter recent divorcee and her partner embark on a cruise to the Great Barrier Reef. Over time, the woman’s disdain for her loud fellow passengers turns to one of admiration and she leaves with a more positive attitude.

title: The Largesse of the Sea Maiden
author: Denis Johnson
logline: An aging ad executive reflects through the years in snapshot scenes about his ex-wives, a troubled friend, an awards ceremony, and an unlikely love story.

title: The Semplica-Girl Diaries
author: George Saunders
logline: A working class man who wants his children to have everything their rich friends have purchases "Semplica Girls" — girls formerly living in poverty who sign contracts to hang as ornaments in people's yards — for his older daughter's birthday. When his younger daughter frees the Semplica Girls, the family is plunged into financial disaster.

title: Night Train to Frankfurt
author: Marisa Silver
logline: Daughter Helen reflects on her pained childhood and strained adult life while on a train in Germany, where she is traveling to Munich with her sick mother to get an unconventional treatment for cancer.

title: The City
author: John Updike
logline: A middle-aged salesman from New Jersey finds himself studying the intricacies of his life and the hospital he stays at after he becomes ill on his flight.

title: The Children Stay
author: Alice Munro
logline: When Pauline’s affair with the director of the amateur production of “Eurydice” turns serious, Pauline leaves her husband in the middle of their vacation, unwittingly leaving her children behind as well.

title: Floating Bridge
author: Alice Munro
logline: Slowly dying from cancer, Jinny wanders to bus stops, cornfields, and to a floating bridge thinking about the futures her husband Neal and many men will have without her.

title: The Scheme of Things
author: Charles D'Ambrosio
logline: A recovered heroin addict begins to doubt that the man she ran away with knows what is best for her future.

title: The Prospectors
author: Karen Russell
logline: Two girls on the run use their wits and charm to steal from wealthy patrons. On their way to yet another party, they make a wrong turn and end up in the company of ghosts who are unaware they were previously killed by a building collapse.

title: You're Ugly, Too
author: Lorrie Moore
logline: American History professor Zoe Hendricks floats through a lonely life unnerving and offending those around her with her odd behavior and unfiltered speech. She flies to New York to visit her sister Evan and meets a prospective suitor, only to reject him in her tempestuous way.

title: The Place To Be
author: Shirley Hazzard
logline: An Australian soldier spends several seasons stationed in a British Imperialist colony in Asia where he interacts with the city’s residents and comes to terms with the evils of imperialism.

title: JunHee
author: Marshall Klimasewiski
logline: A Korean-American immigrant and her husband struggle to process a miscarriage.

title: The Voyage Out
author: John Rolfe Gardiner
logline: During the height of World War II bombings in London, a group of British school boys are sent across the Atlantic to a Canadian boarding school. When one of the boys goes missing from the ship, the school attempts to uncover what really happened during the voyage overseas.

title: Tooth and Claw
author: T.C. Boyle
logline: A young man wins a feral cat from a mysterious stranger at a bar one night and finds his life turned upside-down as he then struggles to care for the cat, overcome his personal insecurities, and love the woman he wants to be with.

title: A Good Loser
author: Elizabeth Cullinan
logline: Ten years after leaving, a woman returns to Ireland and finds her longtime crush now married with children.

title: Certain Hard Places
author: Linda Arking
logline: A young woman reunites with an old college friend who has immersed himself in Marxist ideology and begins falling in love with his deep political passion.

title: Baby Wilson
author: E. L. Doctorow
logline: When his unstable ex girlfriend shows up on his doorstep with a kidnapped baby, a young man must decide what to do with both the baby and the woman.

title: Them Old Cowboy Songs
author: Annie Proulx
logline: A young couple in 1880s Wyoming buys a plot of land, builds a home, and falls in love. The man leaves temporarily for work, but tragedy befalls each of them, and the couple never reunites.

title: The Purchase
author: Elizabeth Hardwick
logline: A seasoned painter in New York is confronted with his senility when a fresh, up-and-coming artist attempts to sell one of his pieces to him. Though the older painter isn't interested in his artwork, he is interested in his fresh, youthful wife.

title: The Man in the Black Suit
author: Stephen King
logline: An old man recalls the day he went fishing as a boy, not long after the death of his brother, and had a terrifying encounter with the Devil.

title: Gunner's Passage
author: Irwin Shaw
logline: American soldiers discuss their lives while waiting for planes to return from a mission.

title: Amundsen
author: Alice Munro
logline: A young woman gets a teaching job at a school for kids who are sick with Tuberculosis, and falls in love with the school doctor.

title: Across the Bridge
author: Mavis Gallant
logline: In mid-20th century Paris, a young woman ends her engagement, hoping to be with another man. When things do not go as planned, however, the young woman struggles to meet both her own wants and desires and her parents' expectations.

title: Differently
author: Alice Munro
logline: A Canadian woman recalls the self-actualization, love, and loss that a recently deceased friend brought into her life throughout their yearslong relationship.

title: Bad Neighbors
author: Edward P. Jones
logline: When a working-class family moves into a middle-class black neighborhood, class prejudices and competition for a young girl’s attention brings the tension between families to an explosive head.

title: Wenlock Edge
author: Alice Munro
logline: A college student gets a roommate who attempts to use her to escape from an abusive relationship with an older man.

title: Once in a Lifetime
author: Jhumpa Lahiri
logline: A young girl grows up hearing stories about close family friends who went back to India, but when the family comes back to America with a secret and lives with her family for a few weeks, tensions erupt.

title: That Last Odd Day in L.A.
author: Ann Beattie
logline: A rich know-it-all visits Los Angeles after his marriage falls apart, where he has a spiritual encounter with wildlife. He is left with a greater understanding of himself, but needs yet another push to finally change his attitude.

title: The Muddle
author: Sana Krasikov
logline: As conflict rages between Russia and Ukraine, a woman struggles to get through to her friend caught in the middle of it.

title: Save My Child!
author: Cynthia Ozick
logline: A Russian emigre calls a long-lost relative in New York asking for asylum. Her strange, self-sabotaging actions call into question her real intentions.

title: Silence
author: Alice Munro
logline: After her college-aged daughter vanishes without saying goodbye, a former Canadian news anchor must rebuild her life. She reckons with her past choices, both personal and professional, which prove to be more than she bargained for.

title: A Wife of Nashville
author: Peter Taylor
logline: After hiring multiple caretakers, one after another, a family finds a near perfect woman whom they adore. However, they are met with a surprise when the caretaker's term comes to an end.

title: A Reasonable Facsimile
author: Jean Stafford
logline: A young pen pal unexpectedly visits a retired professor after their enthusiastic, months-long correspondence. However, their meeting in person goes much less smoothly than their previous communication.

title: Transactions in a Foreign Currency
author: Deborah Eisenberg
logline: A woman travels to see her lover after 6-months of silence. Though she would wish to be in a committed relationship with him, she comes to realize it is not possible and lets him go.

title: Dimension
author: Alice Munro
logline: A woman navigates her new life and her relationship with her criminally insane husband, who killed her three children.

title: The Concert Party
author: Mavis Gallant
logline: A Canadian graduate student and his wife are living in France and often socialize with their peers at concerts and dinner parties. They soon make friends with an established novelist, but as the student continues to meet people he begins to question who he can trust and who his real friends are.

title: Sea Oak
author: George Saunders
logline: A male stripper lives with his unemployed sister and cousin and their kids and his aunt, who remains cheery and optimistic in the face of every ill fortune, in a dangerous neighborhood. Then, his aunt dies and briefly comes back from the dead as a rapidly disintegrating ghoul with magical powers who bosses them around, determined they work toward a better life. He starts to dream of a better future, all the while wondering why others have so much when they have so little.

title: Old Boys, Old Girls
author: Edward P. Jones
logline: A man incarcerated for murder navigates his time behind bars and his reintroduction to the world after being released.

title: Way down Deep in the Jungle
author: Thom Jones
logline: With joints, brawls, and a drunken baboon, head doctor Koestler welcomes two new doctors to an intense African mission.

title: The Gardens of Mont-Saint-Michel
author: William Maxwell
logline: On a vacation in France with his wife and family, Reynolds reminisces about the trip he and his wife took to Mont-Saint Michel decades ago, despairing at the bigger and faster pace of the town and the beauty and culture that seems to have been lost since then.

title: Killing Babies
author: T.C. Boyle
logline: Fresh out of rehab, a recovering addict goes to live with his brother in Detroit who he hasn't seen in six years. He begins working at his brother's obstetrical clinic, where he encounters pro-life protesters that will stop at nothing to get what they want.

title: Post and Beam
author: Alice Munro
logline: A married woman begins a flirtatious affair with her husband's former student, but when her cousin comes to visit, the woman realizes just how much she's sacrificed.

title: Brokeback Mountain
author: Annie Proulx
logline: Two "straight" young men are hired for the summer to look after sheep on Brokeback Mountain; alone together, they fall into a sensual and secret romance that they never forget and can never quite leave behind. Over the next twenty years, although their careers and families threaten to separate them, they find ways to reunite.

title: Defender of the Faith
author: Philip Roth
logline: A WWII army officer begrudgingly sticks his neck out for his fellow Jewish trainees' right to go to shul, which opens him up to manipulations from a trainee who tries to control his fate in the army and avoid deployment in the violent Pacific theater.

title: Wigtime
author: Alice Munro
logline: Two women, once the closest of childhood friends, chart diametrically opposite courses through life when scandal drives them apart. Thirty years later, a chance reunion prompts one of them to question everything.

title: In the Zoo
author: Jean Stafford
logline: Two adult sisters reunite only to relive the trauma from their tumultuous and life-altering childhood.

title: Troy Street
author: Robert Hemenway
logline: A fifty-year-old man from Michigan attempts to interpret a recurring dream about walking around his city with a woman that resembles his wife.

title: A Real Life
author: Alice Munro
logline: In a small rural town in the 1930s, three friends — a farmer’s wife, a music teacher and adulteress, and a single huntswoman — drift away from one another as they grow older, choosing unexpected futures for themselves.

title: The Bear Came Over the Mountain
author: Alice Munro
logline: An old man reflects on his past actions after he puts his wife with Alzheimer’s in a nursing home.

title: Annunciation
author: Lauren Groff
logline: A woman reflects on her time in the Bay Area—and the two women she knew from there.

title: The Schreuderspitze
author: Mark Helprin
logline: After the loss of his wife and son, a young photographer retreats into isolation and sets his focus on training for a challenging mountain climb. He soon becomes consumed by vivid dreams which lead him to face the depths of his grief.

title: The Desert in the Oasis
author: Niccolo Tucci
logline: A married man in New York City must try to get a female friend to reciprocate the love he has for her while helping her through her ongoing separation with her husband.

title: Joshua
author: Shirley Ann Grau
logline: A boy living in poverty in Louisiana needs a winter coat, but can't afford one because his father is too afraid to work.

title: Leaf Season
author: John Updike
logline: A group of five families gather at a farmhouse in Vermont over Columbus Day weekend for their annual vacation. As the weekend drags on, they begin to realize that life has become more complicated and they may be slowly drifting apart.

title: The Important Houses
author: Mary Gordon
logline: Shorty after WWII, a young girl and her mother are forced to move into her grandmother's mysterious and bleak house after her beloved father dies from a heart attack.

title: Passion
author: Alice Munro
logline: An old woman visits the small town where she was once a waitress and remembers how she dated a wealthy college student and built a strong relationship with his intelligent mother. After realizing she didn't want to marry him, she shared a spontaneous, emotionally-intimate drive with his troubled older half-brother, who died by suicide just after.

title: Chance
author: Alice Munro
logline: A young woman makes a detour on her way home to visit a man she met on a train. Though the man is married, the woman hopes to rekindle the spark she felt during the train-ride.

title: The Embarkment for Cythera
author: John Cheever
logline: Discontent with her life, a wealthy woman becomes involved with a young grocery boy, hoping it will spice things up.

title: The Country Husband
author: John Cheever
logline: A bored, neglected husband has a near-death experience that makes him question whether he is truly happy with his life.

title: A House on the Plains
author: E. L. Doctorow
logline: A young man and his widowed mother move to the Midwestern countryside, where the mother runs a deadly get-rich-quick scheme.

title: Heart of Gold
author: Mary Lavin
logline: A woman in Ireland finally gets to be with her long-lost love, but only after he is tragically made a widower when his previous wife passes from an illness, leading the new wife to compare herself to the perfect, kind, dead one.

title: Family Furnishings
author: Alice Munro
logline: A middle-aged Canadian writer reflects on her life, and recalls a family friend who has spent decades drifting in and out of her life, and who leaves chaos and clarity in her wake.

title: Heads of Houses
author: Peter Taylor
logline: While a mid-western US man waits for his family to gather in the car to finally leave his in-law's house, he wanders around the area and thinks about the importance of family, even though he and his father-in-law often disagree on values.

title: Miss Leonora When Last Seen
author: Peter Taylor
logline: When the decision to build a new integrated school falls into the hands of an elderly woman, a small Tennessee town grows desperate to escape the control of her family, which has historically worked to prohibit progress and change.

title: A Silver Dish
author: Saul Bellow
logline: A man thinks back on his late father's thievery, and figures out how to mourn his death.

title: Runaway
author: Alice Munro
logline: Carla's husband pressures her to steal money from her elderly friend, but Carla cannot go through with it. Carla must decide if she should accept her friend's help and run away or confront her temperamental husband.

title: The View from Castle Rock
author: Alice Munro
logline: A Scottish family in the early 1800s spends six weeks on a ship bound for the Americas. Each family member has vastly different experiences as they await their fates across the sea.

title: August
author: Mavis Gallant
logline: A wealthy American divorcée who lives in Paris struggles to maintain her social graces when her adult daughter’s mental health dramatically declines and her marriage deteriorates.

title: Firstborn
author: Larry Woiwode
logline: A couple in Brooklyn is sent into a panic when the pregnant wife begins to have contractions two months early.

title: People Like That Are the Only People Here
author: Lorrie Moore
logline: After finding out that her toddler has cancer, a fiction writer and her husband living in the American Midwest do everything they can to save their baby, including giving up her artistic integrity in order to pay for the medical bills.

title: Tip On A Dead Jockey
author: Irwin Shaw
logline: When a former air force pilot’s friend goes missing for 32 days, he recalls a dangerous but tempting deal he was offered months ago and assumes the worst for his more gullible and perhaps unlucky friend.

title: A Story In An Almost Classical Mode
author: Harold Brodkey
logline: A Harvard College student reflects on his troubled relationship with his mother as she dies.

title: A Long Story Short
author: Shirley Hazzard
logline: A businessman in 1960s London falls passionately in love with his secretary—until he has sex with her.

title: One Summer
author: Mary Lavin
logline: A woman with minimal relationship experience deals with the aftermath of her choice between her first love and her sick father.

title: Carried Away
author: Alice Munro
logline: During World War I, a librarian has her heart broken by a soldier overseas and she tries to overcome her sadness.

title: An Influx of Poets
author: Jean Stafford
logline: The wife of a poet documents her marriage of five years as it tumultuously unravels during one summer in Maine.

title: In the Miro District
author: Peter Taylor
logline: For a teenage boy living in Nashville, Tennessee, it is impossible to be close with his grandfather the way his parents expect them to be. Although they call the same area home, the grandfather and grandson come from opposite worlds.

title: The Remission
author: Mavis Gallant
logline: When a dying Englishman forcefully relocates his family to France for his final resting place, their family falls into disruption during the long years of his unexpected remission.

title: Speck's Idea
author: Mavis Gallant
logline: When an art gallery owner in Paris decides to bring an old, dead painter back into popularity, he must first deal with the painter’s fascist beliefs and manipulative widow.

title: Rosa
author: Cynthia Ozick
logline: Burdened by the memories of her time in Nazi-occupied Poland, a woman destroys her antique shop in New York and moves to Florida, but is still haunted by a persistent researcher and visions of her deceased daughter.

title: Pastoralia
author: George Saunders
logline: A man living full-time as a caveman in a historical exhibit where he isn't supposed to speak English and has to pay for his poop to be removed is pressured by his exploitative employer to report his work partner's violation of their rules, despite knowing that she needs to send her family money as desperately as he does.

title: The Old Forest
author: Peter Taylor
logline: An engaged boy and his girlfriend get into a car accident, after which the girl flees into the woods. The boy is worried that all of this will cause his fiancee to break off their engagement, but instead the couple come together to track down the girl.

title: Puttermesser Paired
author: Cynthia Ozick
logline: In modern day NYC, an unmarried, fifty-something-year-old lawyer takes a year off work to contemplate her fate and plunges into an obsession with the life of the 19th century writer George Eliot—and with recreating Eliot's lifelong love affair.

title: The Love of a Good Woman
author: Alice Munro
logline: A home nurse pieces together the events of a murder after a group of young boys find a dead body in a small Toronto town. She grapples with whether to turn in the murderer—her late patient's husband—and ultimately decides to risk death to confront him directly, with a romantic vision of him turning himself in to relieve his conscience.

title: An interval like this
author: Robert Gorham Davis
logline: Anxious ahead of an important lecture, a psychology professor blows up after finding a photo of his wife's ex-husband.

title: Heavy Snow
author: Han Kang
logline: A woman embarks on a treacherous, snowy journey to help her friend.

title: The Pot of Gold
author: John Cheever
logline: A poor, ever-hopeful couple that imagines itself on the brink of a windfall suffers setback after setback, until the husband has a revelation about what in life holds real value.

title: Labor Day Dinner
author: Alice Munro
logline: A mother, her two children, and their stepfather come over to a friend’s for a dinner on Labor Day.

title: Poor Monsieur Panalitus
author: Kay Boyle
logline: A man of mysterious origins comes under suspicion in a French village when the outbreak of WWII throws his allegiance into question and a death occurs on the grounds of his hotel.

title: The Mud Below
author: Annie Proulx
logline: A 23-year-old man falls deeply in love with bull riding even as the sport destroys his body.

title: Leaving the Church
author: Mark Helprin
logline: Old priest travels to Rome to visit the Vatican, where he sustains an injury sending him into a trip down memory lane.

title: The Pleasures of Travel
author: Wendall Wilcox
logline: Stuck on a train ride with his overbearing wife, a stifled husband questions a fellow passenger about the meaning of love.

title: The Other
author: John Updike
logline: A man's marriage to his college sweetheart is shadowed by his infatuation with her twin sister.

title: Homework
author: Peter Cameron
logline: A disaffected teenager skips school to mourn his dead dog and tries to puzzle out the missing variable in his life.

title: Royal Beatings
author: Alice Munro
logline: At the root of her complicated family formed by her father and stepmother, a girl faces years of abuse through what they consider to be a “royal beating.”

title: I Get By
author: Mary Robison
logline: A widow whose husband died attempting to fly a plane becomes fixated on the compelling young woman hired to replace him as a sixth grade teacher.

title: In the White Night
author: Ann Beattie
logline: En route home from a dinner party with her husband, a woman reflects on the death of their young daughter and the omnipresence of tragedy in their lives.

title: The Fury
author: Robert M. Coates
logline: A disturbed man — consumed by fury at the world and the wickedness he believes it contains — attempts to kidnap a little girl and meets a brutal end.

title: Over By the River
author: William Maxwell
logline: A New York-based family of four, distracted by their own minor inconveniences in life, ignore much more dire situations in the world around them.

title: Vandals
author: Alice Munro
logline: Years after facing abuse from the hermit overseeing a nature preserve, two children—now adults—enact their revenge.

title: The Reverse Bug
author: Lore Segal
logline: A teacher invites her adult students — many with personal ties to the Holocaust — to attend a symposium on genocide, but the event is interrupted by incessant screams of an unknown origin.

title: Sacred Statues
author: William Trevor
logline: Battling poverty, a brilliant but undiscovered statue maker and his pregnant wife try to raise funds for a headstone engraving apprenticeship.

title: Wife-Wooing
author: John Updike
logline: A lustful, rhapsodic husband makes an unsuccessful attempt to seduce his distant wife and is surprised when the tables soon turn.

title: The Cinderella Waltz
author: Ann Beattie
logline: A woman narrates the experience of sending her young daughter off every weekend to stay with her ex-husband and his boyfriend- until things change.
